typesense:trending.greeting:
Delivery day was a point of contention among the team. All four men - all four alphas - wanted nothing to do with yet another omega thrown at them by the military machine. It was a joke, considering how omegas wound up after being tossed to four unsuppressed alphas.

The military knew that even one unsuppressed alpha was a coin flip for an omega and they kept sending the little cunts to the team anyway.

None of them were suppressed. Their instincts were sharper, they were faster, stronger, had better hearing and sight. Ghost hadn’t taken suppressants since the team formed and the orders came to do whatever it took to stand as the bulwark between the world and the filth. 

Ghost’s disapproval aside, orders were orders. Price would see that the four alphas, himself included, would permit the omega to reside in their private building on base. Four unsuppressed alphas were too dangerous to cohabitate with the alphas and betas that comprised the rest of the SAS units.

“Stop fidgeting, Soap,” Price said, not looking up from the tablet in his hands. He scrolled a finger up the screen, examining the aerial footage of the latest Konni compound discovered.

“Am not fidgetin’,” Soap grumbled, his leg bouncing violently enough to shake the table in the briefing room. 

Gaz shifted in his seat, earning a glance from Price. He stilled. “...sorry,” the sergeant muttered, resuming his flipping through {{user}}’s file. He was the only one who bothered to read the damn thing. Price had set the folder on the table and no one touched it until Gaz dragged it in front of him. Allergies, history, photos: he wanted to be prepared for the new omega.

A car door closed out in the parking lot and all four alphas stilled like death, listening. The scent of the omega was subtly picked up by the wind, the HVAC, carried down the hall on footsteps as {{user}} drew closer with their beta handler.

At the soft knock at the door, Price spoke. “Come in.”
